title: Range hood and vent fan

parts.label: Range hood
parts.looks: The canopy or slim box above the cooktop, with switches on the front edge or underside.
parts.normal: Fan runs at each speed and pulls steam up; light works.
parts.abnormal: Fan dead at every speed, grinding or rattling, or smoke drifting past it.

parts.label: Grease filter
parts.looks: The metal mesh or baffle panels underneath the hood.
parts.normal: Light film of grease at most.
parts.abnormal: Thick, dripping grease, or a filter missing.

parts.label: Fan and light switches
parts.looks: The buttons or slide switches on the hood's front edge.
parts.normal: Each press changes the fan speed or light.
parts.abnormal: A stuck or broken button, or no response at all.

parts.label: Hood light
parts.looks: The small bulb or LED panel under the hood that lights the cooktop.
parts.abnormal: Out while the fan still works (often just the bulb).

faults.name: Clogged grease filter (weak suction)
faults.evidence: Thick grease on the filter, with the fan running but steam drifting past the hood.

faults.name: Fan motor or switch failure
faults.evidence: No fan at any speed while the light still works, or a hum without the blades turning. The technician confirms which.

faults.name: Loose fan or damper (rattle)
faults.evidence: A rattle or flapping that changes with fan speed; a noise alone is a description, not proof.

hazards.label: Heavy grease over the burners
hazards.threshold: Thick dripping grease on the hood filters right above the burners. A spoken warning to clean or replace the filters.

may: Pop the grease filters out (most have a finger latch) and show them.
Run the fan at each speed and describe the sound.
Turn the hood off before touching the filters.
must_not: Take the hood off the wall or open its wiring box.
Reach into the fan while it can be switched on.

tour.open: Show me the hood from below, with the filters and switches in view.

checkpoints.hint: Point straight up at the filters. Tap Light if it is dark.
Show me the switches and turn the fan on, low then high.
